# Web Database Layer (apps/web/src/db) — Vida Platform
# Auto-read by Claude when editing files in this directory.
# Generated by AR-2 (LIF-73) · refresh: /layer-docs --refresh

## What this layer is
The browser implementation of `@vida/core`'s `DatabaseAdapter` (AR-2). Runs SQLite in the page via wa-sqlite +
OPFS, off the main thread in a Web Worker, and hands the data layer an async Drizzle instance. Encryption is OFF in
M1.0 (SQLCipher → M3); the seam is pass-through.

## Pattern in use
- **Async everywhere.** wa-sqlite@1.0.0's Factory API is async-only (`step`/`prepare_v2`/`finalize` are `async`), so
  the driver and `DrizzleDb` are asynchronous. `DrizzleDb = SqliteRemoteDatabase<schema>` via `drizzle-orm/sqlite-proxy`.
- **Worker-hosted.** `AccessHandlePoolVFS` needs `FileSystemSyncAccessHandle`, which exists only in a Worker — so the
  engine + driver + Drizzle proxy all live in `worker.ts`. The app-facing main↔worker binding is **`client.ts` (AR-4,
  built 2026-07-30)** — a `WorkerDbClient` shaped as an `SqliteDriver` proxy over the worker RPC; `boot.ts` owns the
  single client + one-time open. `exec`/`values`/`batch` on the client are a deferred seam (throw until entity-CRUD, UI-3/M1.1+).
- **Sync WASM build + AccessHandlePoolVFS** (the non-Asyncify VFS): no SharedArrayBuffer → **no COOP/COEP headers**.
- The proxy callback returns wa-sqlite's positional `row()` arrays; Drizzle maps them (`mapResultRow`) — we never
  import `mapResultRow`.

## Key files
- `web-driver.ts` — async `SqliteDriver` over wa-sqlite's `statements()` iterator (owns prepare/finalize, no leak).
  `query()` → object rows (internal); `values()` → positional arrays (the ORM proxy path).
- `worker.ts` — the Web Worker: bootstraps the VFS, opens, migrates (`ALL_MIGRATIONS` 001–032), builds the Drizzle
  proxy, and exposes an `open|exec|query|close` message protocol (AR-2's in-worker proof).
- `web-adapter.ts` — the `DatabaseAdapter` impl (`open`/`migrate`/`createDrizzle`/`exists`/`destroy`). `exists`/`destroy`
  are VFS-directory-scoped (the VFS stores files under opaque OPFS names); per-name first-run detection is AR-4.
- `wa-sqlite-vendor.d.ts` — ambient type shim for `AccessHandlePoolVFS` (ships as JS with no `.d.ts`).
- `web-adapter.test.ts` — Node contract test: drives the real `createDrizzleProxy` over a better-sqlite3 stand-in
  (proves the row-shape contract), migrate no-op + failing-migration rollback, and the encryption seam.

## Conventions / gotchas
- Adapter/driver/proxy contracts are owned by `@vida/core/src/db/adapter.ts` — this layer only implements them.
- `createDrizzleProxy` (in `@vida/core`) is the shared SQL→driver mapping; `web-adapter.createDrizzle` delegates to it.
- OPFS/worker wiring can't be unit-tested in jsdom (`FileSystemSyncAccessHandle` is browser-worker-only) → a Playwright
  smoke is the follow-up; the Node/better-sqlite3 split proves the contract.
- Repository CRUD is DB-6's surface. Field-level **encryption** (`encryptField`/`decryptField`) needs an UNLOCKED vault
  (a password-derived key → M3), and is skipped for empty-`[E]` repos (M1.0 pass-through). **But every WRITE also
  computes a keyless `_sync_hash` via `hashContent()` → that requires `initVault()` (libsodium WASM loaded) at boot,
  independent of `[E]`.** MOD-notes ②a exercises repository writes on web (no unlock); `db/boot.ts` calls `initVault()`.
  See `docs/specs/fixes/vault-not-initialized-on-boot` (+ a follow-up to hoist libsodium-ready into @vida/core's open path).
